subject: GPU runway & deal commitments — playbook (ACME POC)
messages:
From: Riya Shah <riya.shah@acme.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing for ACME edge POC + timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency profile. We're trying to flush out what we should commit to for a Q4 pilot (internal exec asks). High level:
- Pilot expected to run for 8 weeks with ~40 concurrent sessions at peak.
- Model family: 13B-ish open model (we'll provide exact weights).
- Preferred: dedicated GPUs for predictable latency; we'll consider burst for spikes.

Can you send a quick playbook with suggested committed sizing, options for burst, and an outline of procurement steps (SOW/PO timing + finance contacts)? We need rough numbers by next week so execs can sign off.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Riya Shah
Director, Edge AI
Acme Robotics

Attachments: none
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Riya Shah <riya.shah@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing for ACME edge POC + timeline

Thanks Riya — great to see this moving forward. I put together a short playbook template so we can align internal stakeholders quickly. Highlights below, full template attached.

High-level recommendation (starter):
- Committed baseline: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs for the 8-week pilot (predictable throughput for 40 concurrent sessions, 2k token sequences).
- Burst buffer: +2 GPUs available on-demand for spikes (rules-based burst, billed separately).
- Autoscale ramp: start with 4 active and scale to 6 over first 2 weeks as traffic stabilizes.

What I need from Acme: final model size, expected qps distribution, and any hard latency SLOs.

Next steps:
1) Laura to sync deal milestone & target commit window.
2) Ben to scope preliminary commit spend options and billing cadence.
3) Monica to confirm infra feasibility and slot booking.

Attaching: ACME_POC_capacity_template.xlsx (simple workbook: demand by week, tier mapping, and cost estimate).

Happy to schedule a 30-min alignment this week.

—
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Thanks Jonas / Riya — looping in some forecast context from GTM so infra & finance can map to risk. Key pipeline notes:
- ACME POC target close: 2028-10-15 (exec decision window).
- Probability-weighted ARR if converted: $1.2M ARR (50% conv. assumed for forecast).
- Useful to evaluate two commitment tiers for commercial: 6-GPU pilot (recommended) and 12-GPU reserved if they push for production after POC.

Milestones / asks for this thread:
- Confirm baseline commit for pilot (6 GPUs) and whether Acme will accept monthly reserved billing or needs quarterly invoices.
- Ben: can you draft two quick pricing sketches (monthly reserved w/ discount vs pay-as-you-go + burst)?
- Monica: please confirm whether the infra team can guarantee slot reservation in our West region for the Oct window and what lead time for procurement is.

I'll book the cross-functional 30-min sync for Friday; agenda: sizing, pricing sketches, procurement steps, and a short list of required PO docs.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 7 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing for ACME edge POC + timeline

On Thu, Jul 5, 2028 at 11:30 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll book the cross-functional 30-min sync for Friday; agenda: sizing, pricing sketches, procurement steps, and a short list of required PO docs.

Thanks — quick infra read and recommendation:
- Feasibility: West region has capacity but we need a 6-week lead to guarantee reserved slots for Oct.
- Technical sizing: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs should cover 40 concurrent sessions at 2k tokens with prefix cache enabled. If they plan to run larger models (20B+), we should re-evaluate.
- Burst: +2 GPUs as burst (pre-warmed KV-cache policy) is feasible; recommend conservative burst policy (max 2 concurrent burst GPUs, 1-hour billing granularity).

Operational implications:
- Commit run-rate impact: 6 GPUs reserved for 8 weeks ~= 336 GPU-hours/week — finance will need this for runway forecasting.
- Lead-time: procurement & onboarding (SLA + network peering) = ~4 weeks after PO receipt.

Attaching a short runway estimate for the pilot.

Monica Patel
Fleet & Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Thanks team — summarizing agreed actions and owners ahead of the weekly fleet planning slot (Wed 10am PT):
1) Confirmed baseline pilot sizing: 6 reserved GPUs + 2 burst GPUs (Monica to add to slot calendar; lead-time noted).
2) Finance to produce two pricing sketches (Ben) by EOD Tuesday: monthly reserved vs PAYG + burst.
3) Sales to secure a PO window and preferred billing cadence (Laura / Jonas).
4) Engineering to validate final model memory and QPS when Acme shares weights (Jonas to collect).
5) Legal/procurement checklist: standard SOW + PO terms — Laura to pull the template.

KPI to track in the weekly fleet sync: reserved GPU-hours committed vs. available, projected run-rate impact, and any region contention flags. Monica — please surface any slot conflicts in the West region by the Tuesday checkpoint.

Riya — can you confirm if Acme requires an on-prem/air-gapped assessment or if public VPC Dedicated is fine? That will change lead time materially.

I'll run the 10am weekly beam in fleet planning and invite the extended stakeholders.
